status: parsimonious theoretical and methodological framework; no human validation yet
novelty_position: Integration and empirical testing of an explicit temporal attachment-regulation sequence in adult romantic relationships; not a new control-system architecture.

h1_model_set.M2: M0 + perceived state r_hat_t + desired state r_star_t as unconstrained separate predictors
h1_model_set.M3: M0 + signed discrepancy e_t = r_star_t - r_hat_t; primary ARC discrepancy representation
h1_model_set.M4: M0 + positive discrepancy + negative discrepancy; prespecified asymmetry extension

discrepancy_logic.primary_inference: co-primary coefficient-first tests rather than sequential predictive gating
discrepancy_logic.H1_P1: one-sided Wald test H0: M2 within-person beta_r_star <= 0.5 versus beta_r_star > 0.5, Holm-controlled with H1-P2
discrepancy_logic.H1_P2: one-sided Wald test H0: M3 within-person beta_e <= 0.5 versus beta_e > 0.5, Holm-controlled with H1-P1
discrepancy_logic.multiplicity: Holm family-wise alpha 0.05 across the two one-sided SESOI tests
discrepancy_logic.asymmetry_contrast: d_asym = beta_positive + beta_negative, where beta_negative multiplies max(-e,0)
discrepancy_logic.predictive_role: participant-paired temporal-holdout RMSE is secondary evidence and does not gate evaluation of M2, M3, or M4
discrepancy_logic.no_forced_winner: M2, M3, and M4 are reported as a structural evidence profile rather than forced into one mandatory winner
discrepancy_logic.interpretation_limit: H1-P2 alone does not establish information beyond perceived state; joint H1-P1/H1-P2 support does not uniquely identify a psychological mechanism
discrepancy_logic.asymmetry_role: secondary descriptive structural evidence; focused N=84 validation rejected all prespecified confirmatory tolerance candidates

target_drift.implication: discrepancy reduction can occur through relational-state change, target change, or both
target_drift.rule: retain perceived and desired states separately even when discrepancy is the primary predictor

recovery.status: multidimensional outcome, not a single latent index
candidate_metrics: discrepancy burden: sum |e_t| * delta_t after a perturbation
relative contribution of state change versus target change

h3_hierarchy.R1: R0 + attachment anxiety L + attachment avoidance U
h3_hierarchy.R2: R1 + positive secure-base representation S; decisive H3 increment
h3_hierarchy.R3: R2 + proximal perceived/observed partner support or dyadic coping

h3_rules: S is not required by the current ARC core
each confirmatory H3 study nominates one primary recovery endpoint before data inspection; the endpoint must not count target retreat alone as successful recovery
promotion requires incremental value beyond L/U on the primary recovery endpoint and genuinely out-of-sample predictive improvement
promotion requires independent replication or a second preregistered design supporting the increment
secondary recovery metrics provide convergent evidence but cannot rescue failure on the primary endpoint
if S loses value after proximal support is added, report attenuation conditional on support; do not infer mediation or automatically promote S
if proximal support predicts recovery but S does not, retain S outside the core and simplify toward episode-level coregulation

core_hypotheses: H1 desired-state information contributes to subsequent regulation beyond perceived state/context/history, and signed desired-minus-perceived discrepancy predicts subsequent action; representation symmetry/asymmetry is tested with prespecified structural contrasts
H2 attachment anxiety and avoidance moderate channel-specific discrepancy-to-action mappings across approach, distance, and internal regulation
extension_hypotheses: H4 mentalized affectivity and emotion-regulation flexibility add pathway-specific moderation only if discriminant and incremental validity are supported
H5 preregistered dynamic indicators improve held-out prediction of independently measured adult disorganization beyond static attachment baselines

M.name: mentalized affectivity
M.role: optional predictor/moderator of externally scored state-inference quality

F.name: emotion-regulation flexibility
F.role: optional predictor/moderator of context- and feedback-sensitive policy adaptation

validation_rules: feature engineering and all confirmatory thresholds must not use the final temporal test block
H1 primary inference uses direct coefficient tests with Holm multiplicity control; holdout RMSE is secondary evidence rather than a sequential gate
evaluate later observations within known people and generalization to held-out people separately
the simple difference score is a testable restriction rather than a preprocessing fact
added dynamic structure is retained only with reproducible held-out or external-validity improvement
successful temporal prediction does not uniquely identify an underlying computational mechanism
H2 must be tested on component action channels, not only a signed action summary
H3 is a promotion test for candidate S rather than a protected core assumption

S is promoted to required core status only after improvement beyond L/U on a preregistered primary recovery endpoint, genuinely out-of-sample predictive value, and independent replication or a second preregistered design

disorganization.status: external extension, not a core latent state
disorganization.rule: do not equate high L+U, raw variability, or a simulator index with disorganization

h2_policy.status: core extension after H1 measurement viability
action_channels: overt distancing/space seeking; not a direct measure of autonomy
h2_policy.model: a_k(t+1) = alpha_k_i + beta_e_k e_wp_t + gamma_L_k L_i*e_wp_t + gamma_U_k U_i*e_wp_t + phi_k_i a_k_t + beta_c_k c_t + error
key_logic: attachment dimensions may alter both response magnitude and response channel
signed action is insufficient for H2 because high approach and high distance can cancel
autonomy denotes experienced volition and must be measured separately; distancing alone does not establish autonomy satisfaction or attachment avoidance
strongest directional expectation concerns positive discrepancy / closeness deficit
H2 requires a design powered for cross-level moderation and random-slope heterogeneity
falsification: remove ARC-specific dynamic role if L/U do not reproducibly moderate within-person discrepancy-to-channel mappings
do not treat between-person mean action differences alone as H2 support
do not retain interactions that fail replication or held-out predictive improvement

S.name: secure-base representation
S.status: prespecified candidate for promotion to the person-level core
S.rationale: positive security has an independent theoretical and measurement tradition, but ARC-specific incremental recovery validity beyond L/U is not yet established
S.promotion_rule: promote only after S adds reproducible information for a preregistered primary recovery outcome beyond L/U, improves genuinely out-of-sample prediction, and the increment is independently replicated or supported by a second preregistered design; stronger evidence requires persistence after proximal partner support or dyadic coping is modeled
S.no_promotion_rule: if S adds no recovery information beyond L/U, it remains outside the required core; if its increment disappears after proximal support, report attenuation conditional on support rather than identified mediation

candidate_core_hypothesis.H3: positive secure-base representation S earns promotion to the person-level core only if it improves a preregistered primary recovery outcome beyond L/U, adds genuinely out-of-sample predictive value, and the increment is independently replicated or supported by a second preregistered design; stronger tests add proximal partner support

acronym_semantics: Control refers to feedback-based regulation toward relational goals in the control-theoretic sense, not interpersonal dominance, coercion, or a generalized need for control.
